name: Archdiocese of Philadelphia

base: The most clerical diocese in the country: a seminary that once held five hundred men, a school system that once held a quarter million children, and a presbyterate that still calls the archbishop 'the Cardinal' whether he is one or not.

Rowhouse parishes a mile apart, each with a school, a convent, and a hall, built by the Irish, the Italians, the Poles, and the Germans, and now half-closed and half-Latino, Vietnamese, and West African.
Two saints are buried here, a third was born here, and the presbyterate is quietly certain that the American Church was invented on Logan Square.

byNeed.critically_short: Ordination classes of four for a diocese built for forty, and mergers announced in batches of ten.
byNeed.stretched: Pastors cover two rowhouse parishes and a shrine and learn which one has the boiler that will fail first.
byNeed.adequate: The seminary in Gwynedd is small but full, and the Vietnamese and Nigerian priests fill what the Irish cannot.
byNeed.deep_bench: More priests than anyone expected, and a personnel board that can afford to keep a difficult man in a small parish for years.

byFinancial.healthy: The Main Line pays for the city: the parishes of Villanova and Bryn Mawr are the endowment, and know it.
byFinancial.strained: Two hundred schools became a hundred, and the parishes that kept theirs are running on the sales of the ones that closed.
byFinancial.crisis: The settlements, the pensions, and the schools came due at once, and the archbishop has sold the seminary grounds and the cardinal's residence.

byTension.one_voice: The presbyterate is careful, old, and Irish, and does not argue in public.
byTension.quietly_split: Split between the men of the old seminary, who ran the diocese, and the men of the new one, who will.
byTension.openly_divided: The grand jury reports have never stopped, the men who were named are known to everyone, and the argument about who protected them is conducted in the pews.

complications: A grand jury report that named names, and a presbyterate in which every man over sixty knew someone on the list.
A school system that was the largest in the country and is closing a dozen schools a year, each closing a parish's reason to exist.
A seminary that moved out of its landmark grounds, and an alumni body that has not forgiven it.
Two shrines, a basilica, and a cathedral within three miles of each other, each with a pastor who thinks he outranks the others.
hiddenComplications: A monsignor at the chancery who was the secretary for clergy through the worst years and has never been indicted.
The archbishop has been told which parishes will merge next and has told the pastors nothing.
A Main Line parish's endowment that has been quietly lent to the chancery and not repaid.

weather: Winter is a grey slush from Advent to Lent, and the rowhouse church's boiler is a topic at every parish council.
Spring comes in a week in April and the whole diocese schedules its Confirmations in it.
Summer is a wet heat that empties the city for the Shore, and the pastor learns which weekends the collection will be half.
October is the one month the city is beautiful without effort, and the Eagles decide the mood of the Sunday Masses.
sunday: The eight o'clock in South Philadelphia is Italian widows and a Vietnamese family in the front pew; the noon Mass in Kensington is Spanish and full.
On the Main Line the ushers are lawyers and the collection is by envelope and app; in Chester it is cash and a second collection for someone's rent.
Everyone gives directions by parish here, and a man from Mayfair told you where he lives by naming three churches, two of them closed.
presbyterate: The priests of Philadelphia call every archbishop 'the Cardinal' and every classmate by his year, and know which years were the good ones.
Half of them went to Overbrook and the other half to Gwynedd, and the difference shows at dinner in the way they hold a fork.
They know every closed church by name and can tell you what it is now: condos, a charter school, a Baptist congregation that kept the statues.
